data.note:
Reflection: I called Microtubule stabilizers, truth is Protein degradation (MG-132, PubChem CID 462382, structure agrees; ChEMBL CHEMBL64925 has no curated mechanism).

Why I missed: 3/4 wells showed bright diffuse tubulin (tub_mean z +14 to +116), high tubulin texture, small round solid cells, green-dominant composite - the Microscopist and atlas both pointed to stabilizers. But per-well NSC was split 2-2 stabilizers vs actin disruptors with low similarities 0.38-0.47, i.e. weak evidence, and the 30 uM well was a toxic collapse (tiny shrunken nuclei, negative tubulin). I discounted that as toxicity and locked on stabilizers, dropping Protein degradation from the board early.

Lesson: proteasome inhibition causes accumulation/arrest phenotypes - rounded mitotic-like cells with intense tubulin - that mimic stabilization in a 3-stain panel without a specific degradation readout. Literature confirms MG-132 is a proteasome inhibitor inducing apoptosis/stress responses e.g. PMID 21499287, PMID 21203833, PMID 30695709. With a tied low-similarity NSC vote I should have retained Protein degradation and noted the library has few such references. Follow-up I proposed (tubulin polymerization + acetyl-tubulin + p-H3) would still discriminate, plus ubiquitin/proteasome activity assay.

reflection.text:
We called Microtubule stabilizers because three wells replicated a tubulin-bright, rounded phenotype: e2 tub_mean z=+54.7, tub_glcm_contrast z=+151.7 at 3 uM, e7 tub_mean z=+14.2 at 3 uM rep2, and e8 tub_mean z=+116.4, contrast z=+328.0 at 10 uM, with microscopist support in e5. We discounted e3 at 30 uM with nuc_solidity z=-414.8 and similarity 0.265 as segmentation failure/debris, and raised stabilizers to 0.78 despite a split NSC vote of 2/4 and non-monotonic dose_response rho=-0.32 p=0.68 in e10.

Unblinding to MG-132, a proteasome inhibitor that induces apoptosis via oxidative stress (PMID 21499287) and modulates ERK/Akt/mTOR survival signaling (PMID 21203833), also studied for anti-inflammatory proteasome inhibition (PMID 36791578), shows the tubulin signal was secondary. Proteasome blockade with cell rounding, mitotic delay and apoptosis can condense and brighten tubulin staining and increase texture contrast, mimicking stabilization without direct tubulin binding.

The error was interpretive and design-driven: the reference atlas contained no Protein degradation class, so 1-NN voting could never return the truth, and per-well results were actually tied 2 stabilizer vs 2 Actin disruptor with summed similarities 0.856 vs 0.728. By acquiring only 3, 10 and 30 uM and treating divergent high-dose calls as toxicity, we confirmed our prior instead of testing a proteasome hypothesis with low doses or ubiquitin/proteasome readouts.
what_was_right: Replicated tubulin intensity and texture increase at 3 uM in two wells (e2 tub_mean z=+54.7, contrast z=+151.7; e7 tub_mean z=+14.2, contrast z=+28.9) and at 10 uM (e8 tub_mean z=+116.4, contrast z=+328.0), showing the signal was not single-well noise.
Flagged e3 30 uM as unreliable toxic collapse with extreme nuclear features (nuc_solidity z=-414.8, n=410 objects) and lowest similarity 0.265 versus 0.386-0.47 for the 3 uM wells.

Recognized uncertainty via split atlas evidence (NSC 2/4 stabilizers, k-neighbours 5/10 stabilizers, 3/10 destabilizers) and flat dose_response (tub_mean rho=-0.32 p=0.68, cell_count rho=+0.32 p=0.68).
what_was_wrong: Interpreted increased tub_mean and tub_glcm_contrast as direct microtubule stabilization, missing that MG-132 proteasome inhibition secondarily causes rounded, condensed tubulin-bright mitotic/apoptotic cells.
Dismissed the two Actin disruptor 1-NN calls at 30 uM (similarity 0.265) and 10 uM (similarity 0.463) as debris rather than evidence that the phenotype did not stably match stabilizers.

Chose only mid-high doses (3, 10, 30 uM) with replicate plus bridging dose and no low-dose curve or proteasome-specific measurement, while using an atlas with no Protein degradation class so the true MoA was un votable.

citations.claim: MG-132 acts as a proteasome inhibitor that induces C6 glioma cell apoptosis via oxidative stress (PMID 21499287).
Proteasome inhibition by MG-132 alters cell survival signaling through down-regulation of ERK and Akt/mTOR pathways (PMID 21203833).
MG-132 is studied as a proteasome inhibitor with anti-inflammatory effects in acute injury models (PMID 36791578).

reflection.next_experiment: Test 20S proteasome activity with a fluorogenic peptide substrate plus ubiquitin-conjugate Western blot across the same 0.03-100 uM range, with paclitaxel and bortezomib/MG-132 controls and counter-readouts of acetylated tubulin and phospho-H3 to determine if tubulin brightness is secondary mitotic arrest/proteotoxic rounding rather than direct stabilization.

## Conclusion

**Microtubule stabilizers** (stated probability 0.78); key evidence e2, e5, e7, e8, e9.

Why: Three wells show tubulin-bright rounding; split NSC vote resolved to stabilizers as 30uM is low-similarity toxic collapse.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: In vitro tubulin polymerization assay plus acetylated-tubulin IF and phospho-H3 mitotic index dose curve to confirm stabilization vs destabilization.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

APPROVE. Tubulin increase replicated in two 3 uM wells (dose 4, tub_mean z=+54.7 and +14.2; contrast +151.7 and +28.9) and 10 uM (dose 5, +116.4/+328.0). Actin disruptors are not favored (actin near control in replicate), and microtubule destabilizers predict tubulin loss, opposite to observed. NSC atlas is split 2/2, but the quantitative tubulin signal is decisive. The 30 uM well is unreliable due to segmentation failure (462 vs 2 nuclei, extreme nuclear collapse, n=410 debris). Acquisitions were discriminative (replicate + bridging dose). 10 uM is single-well n=14, but not sole basis; 0.78 is calibrated. Budget exhausted; no free analysis would change this.

## Unblinding

Compound: **MG-132** (PubChem CID [462382](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/462382))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: the call was **Microtubule stabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Protein degradation**.

## Reflection

We called Microtubule stabilizers because three wells replicated a tubulin-bright, rounded phenotype: e2 tub_mean z=+54.7, tub_glcm_contrast z=+151.7 at 3 uM, e7 tub_mean z=+14.2 at 3 uM rep2, and e8 tub_mean z=+116.4, contrast z=+328.0 at 10 uM, with microscopist support in e5. We discounted e3 at 30 uM with nuc_solidity z=-414.8 and similarity 0.265 as segmentation failure/debris, and raised stabilizers to 0.78 despite a split NSC vote of 2/4 and non-monotonic dose_response rho=-0.32 p=0.68 in e10.

Unblinding to MG-132, a proteasome inhibitor that induces apoptosis via oxidative stress (PMID 21499287) and modulates ERK/Akt/mTOR survival signaling (PMID 21203833), also studied for anti-inflammatory proteasome inhibition (PMID 36791578), shows the tubulin signal was secondary. Proteasome blockade with cell rounding, mitotic delay and apoptosis can condense and brighten tubulin staining and increase texture contrast, mimicking stabilization without direct tubulin binding.

The error was interpretive and design-driven: the reference atlas contained no Protein degradation class, so 1-NN voting could never return the truth, and per-well results were actually tied 2 stabilizer vs 2 Actin disruptor with summed similarities 0.856 vs 0.728. By acquiring only 3, 10 and 30 uM and treating divergent high-dose calls as toxicity, we confirmed our prior instead of testing a proteasome hypothesis with low doses or ubiquitin/proteasome readouts.

What was right:
- Replicated tubulin intensity and texture increase at 3 uM in two wells (e2 tub_mean z=+54.7, contrast z=+151.7; e7 tub_mean z=+14.2, contrast z=+28.9) and at 10 uM (e8 tub_mean z=+116.4, contrast z=+328.0), showing the signal was not single-well noise.
- Flagged e3 30 uM as unreliable toxic collapse with extreme nuclear features (nuc_solidity z=-414.8, n=410 objects) and lowest similarity 0.265 versus 0.386-0.47 for the 3 uM wells.
- Recognized uncertainty via split atlas evidence (NSC 2/4 stabilizers, k-neighbours 5/10 stabilizers, 3/10 destabilizers) and flat dose_response (tub_mean rho=-0.32 p=0.68, cell_count rho=+0.32 p=0.68).

What was wrong or missed:
- Interpreted increased tub_mean and tub_glcm_contrast as direct microtubule stabilization, missing that MG-132 proteasome inhibition secondarily causes rounded, condensed tubulin-bright mitotic/apoptotic cells.
- Dismissed the two Actin disruptor 1-NN calls at 30 uM (similarity 0.265) and 10 uM (similarity 0.463) as debris rather than evidence that the phenotype did not stably match stabilizers.
- Chose only mid-high doses (3, 10, 30 uM) with replicate plus bridging dose and no low-dose curve or proteasome-specific measurement, while using an atlas with no Protein degradation class so the true MoA was un votable.

Proposed next experiment: Test 20S proteasome activity with a fluorogenic peptide substrate plus ubiquitin-conjugate Western blot across the same 0.03-100 uM range, with paclitaxel and bortezomib/MG-132 controls and counter-readouts of acetylated tubulin and phospho-H3 to determine if tubulin brightness is secondary mitotic arrest/proteotoxic rounding rather than direct stabilization.

Citations verified: 3/3

- PMID [21499287](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21499287/): Proteasome inhibitor MG-132 induces C6 glioma cell apoptosis via oxidative stress. *Acta Pharmacol Sin* (2011) — MG-132 acts as a proteasome inhibitor that induces C6 glioma cell apoptosis via oxidative stress (PMID 21499287).

- PMID [36791578](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36791578/): Molecular mechanism of anti-inflammatory effects of the proteasome inhibitor MG-132 on Con A-induced acute liver injury in mice. *Res Vet Sci* (2023) — MG-132 is studied as a proteasome inhibitor with anti-inflammatory effects in acute injury models (PMID 36791578).
